newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul buyers seen seeking more Canadian feed wheat.
newsitem.headline: Seoul buyers seen seeking more Canadian feed wheat.

text.p: South Korean feed millers are expected to buy substantially more Canadian feed wheat for shipment from March, 1997 if prices continue falling to levels close to those of imported corn, traders said on Tuesday.
"Our clients' interest in Canadian feed wheat has recently increased," said a local agent for a major foreign supplier.
He said several South Korean buyers were ready to buy Canadian feed wheat in place of U.S. corn if the Canadian grain price was comparatively lower.
The current U.S. corn price to South Korea is around $162 a tonne C&F for May-June shipment next year, while Argentine corn is quoted at about $152-$154 C&F for June shipment.

"The latest purchases by local companies have shown Canadian feed wheat quoted at $162.80 a tonne on a cost and freight basis. It was lower than Indian feed wheat which is currently quoted at $185 a tonne," said Lee Young-ho, a local agent for a Canadian grain exporter.

"If Canadian feed wheat prices are quoted around the level of U.S. corn prices, Korean buyers will move to fill their needs for shipment next year from March onwards," Lee said. "But we can not estimate the volume of how much will be purchased. It depends on how corn prices move."
According to the traders' data obtained by Reuters, South Korea's total feed wheat deals amounted to at least 862,500 tonnes this year.
Canadian feed wheat purchases totalled about 338,000 tonnes, compared with 219,000 tonnes of Indian feed wheat purchases.

"If Canadian wheat prices are lower than that of U.S. corn, we will buy some. This year we have already purchased four 50,000-tonne cargoes of Canadian feed wheat," said an official at the National Livestock Cooperative Federation.
But South Korea's corn purchases will still dwarf those of feed wheat with the country expected to import around nine million tonnes this year, mainly from the U.S. -- the world's largest exporter.
Local traders said any additional feed wheat will be mixed with corn in animal feed.
